observations.content: Bootstrapped Doxa's standard landing-gate infrastructure for this repo: KG Guard + Claude Code Review GitHub Actions workflows, kg-save-gate/review-gate/test-gate PreToolUse hooks, session-start-kg-import + pre-compact-kg-export hooks, attest-review.sh + knowledge-graph-merkle.cjs (CommonJS, this repo's package.json has type:module), and this initial .knowledge-graph/graph.json. Ported from openclaw's landing-gates suite per doxa-cns CLAUDE.md PR-visibility/bank-the-gold/kg-save-on-every-merge doctrine. claude-code-review.yml's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret is NOT yet configured on GitHub — workflow is inert until Garth adds it.

claude-code-review.yml (just added in #14) copied the pre-fix openclaw template's if: condition referencing github.event.pull_request.* while the trigger is workflow_dispatch only, which always evaluates false. Confirmed by an async /code-review that returned after #14 merged. Same bug independently fixed the same day in doxa-cns, openclaw, and doxa-shared.
Propagated the 2026-08-11 atomic-write and --type-guard fixes from doxa-cns's canonical knowledge-graph-merkle.js.

Ported the merge-resolve tool + mechanical merge-integrity guard from doxa-cns's canonical knowledge-graph-merkle.js (2026-08-13, Garth: 'standing doctrine and practice across all repos'). Used it to actually resolve this repo's own stalled PR #15 conflict (which had gone unmerged since 2026-08-11 for the same class of reason this guard exists to prevent).

Hardened per /code-review high findings (doxa-cns 2026-08-13, ported via feat/kg-merge-resolve): (1) PLACEMENT — the merge-integrity check was unreachable from the mcp__github__merge_pull_request landing path (a separate branch that never extracts .tool_input.command), so it was added to run unconditionally at the top of that branch too, before its own PR-diff fast path. (2) check-kg-merge-integrity.cjs now wraps main() in try/catch and fails OPEN (exit 0) on any internal error instead of exit 1, which was indistinguishable from a confirmed violation. (3) observationsAt() now requires a non-empty string hash, so malformed observations are skipped instead of collapsing onto one Map key. (4) mergeResolve()'s sort now breaks timestamp ties by hash, making the result truly order-independent. (5) mergeResolve() guards JSON.parse with try/catch for friendly errors, and gained test coverage (tests/merge-resolve.test.cjs, tests/kg-save-gate-merge-integrity.test.cjs). Also fixed package.json's npm test glob, which was silently never running tests/check-kg-merge-integrity.test.cjs (a .cjs file the tests/**/*.test.js glob can't match) — the existing test had zero real coverage until this fix.

Fix round for /code-review high findings on the hardening PR itself (2026-08-13): (1) the two independent kg-save-gate.sh copies of the merge-integrity check had already diverged (only one validated repo identity) — collapsed into one shared check_kg_merge_integrity() function, called from both the MCP-merge and Bash-command landing paths, now with a git-common-dir identity guard so a drifted persistent cwd can't point the check at the wrong repo. (2) observationsAt() in check-kg-merge-integrity.cjs had its try/catch narrowed to JSON.parse only, so a valid-JSON-wrong-shape blob (e.g. literal null) threw past the function and aborted the whole merge-commit loop instead of fail-opening for just that ref — restored one try/catch around parse+map-build. (3) mergeResolve()'s onlyInOurs/onlyInTheirs counts used raw ours.length/theirs.length, undercounting (sometimes to 0, suppressing the message) when a malformed entry on one side wasn't matched on the other — now computed from per-side valid-hash Sets. (4) mergeResolve() parsed ours/theirs but didn't guard against a valid-JSON non-object (e.g. null), which threw an uncaught TypeError on .observations access — the exact raw-stack-trace failure the JSON.parse guard was meant to eliminate; added an explicit object-shape check with a friendly error.

The kg-guard job now carries an explicit 'name: KG Guard'. Without it the job reports its check-run under the bare job id 'check' — which is what a branch ruleset's required-status-check has to match on, so requiring it was both ambiguous (any other workflow with a job id 'check' collides) and unreadable in the PR checks list. Prerequisite for the 2026-08-15 fleet-wide enforcement pass: KG Guard ran on PRs in every repo but was a REQUIRED check in none of them, so the banking doctrine rested entirely on the merger choosing to wait for green — the local .claude/hooks/kg-save-gate.sh only binds Claude sessions in that checkout, and web-UI merges bypass everything.

demo/ is deployed with Vercel, so a .vercel/ directory appears there on every local deploy. demo/.gitignore keeps it out of the tree — it was sitting untracked and unbanked until the 2026-09-02 fleet sweep.
